_doc: THE SHIFT REGISTER (ARCH-COMPOSED-PROSE §8.6; lane SEAM car 4). EVERY MECHANISM WHOSE CHANGE RE-ROLLS A DRAWN INDEX, each with its PIN, its DOOR and its declared-row idiom. THE PROMISE (W3): a FACT shift is forbidden; a TEXT shift is declared and owner-signed. v1 of the architecture declared two shifts and carried at least three more undeclared, which is the failure this file exists to make impossible: a mechanism absent from this register is a same-seed text shift nobody signed. Consumed by tests/data/dossierStateProseProjection.contract.test.js, which PRINTS the register and RECOMPUTES every pin from the leaves themselves. Nothing reads this at runtime and nothing ships it.
_pinIdiom: A PIN IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A PROMISE. Each row's `pin` is recomputed by the contract test from the committed leaves (`integer` and `map` compared directly, `digest` re-derived over the named material, `source` asserted as a substring of the named file), so a mechanism that moves without its row moving reds NAMING THE MECHANISM. A car that intends the move edits the row IN THE SAME COMMIT as the change and records the shift class; a car that did not intend it has just been told. This is the `.prose-byte-baseline.json` declared-row idiom applied to draw mechanisms instead of bytes.
_digestMaterial: Every `digest` pin is sha256 over one line per pool, the pools ordered by `${block} :: ${pool}` ascending, joined by a single newline with no trailing newline. The line is `${block} :: ${pool} :: ${value}` except for `pool-key-rename`, whose line is `${block} :: ${pool}` alone, and for `norm-bit`, whose line is `${blockId}::${poolKey} ${departure}` over the norm leaf's own rows in key order. A digest is used wherever the mechanism is per-pool: 708 integers cannot be read by a person, and a digest that moves names the mechanism while the diff names the pool.
_shiftClasses: ARCH §8.6 declares FOUR text-shift classes and nothing else re-rolls a drawn index: 1 the REWRITE + FACES freeze (car 8a-8n, one owner re-record); 2 the list-position keys (car 10); 3 THIN-pool growth (car 9b); 4 TURNS (car 11). Each row below names the class it would land under. A row whose `shift` is `none` names a mechanism that must NEVER move: a renumbering, and a pool-key rename.

notMechanisms.what: poolMeta.readsCount — the census's field count for the pool's selecting branch, carried in the RENDER half so the composer can spend the fact budget `k <= 3 - |spine.reads|` (the car-3a ADDENDUM's ruling)
notMechanisms.why: IT IS NOT A MECHANISM OF THIS REGISTER, and it is named here so that absence reads as a decision rather than an oversight. It is an integer the composer spends a BUDGET against; it is not a modulus, not a key, not an ordering and not an eligibility test, so no value of it can move a drawn index. It moves only when the census re-measures what a pool's branch reads, which is a WIRING fact and reds at the census's own `--check` interlock; the projector reads it from the census and never derives it. Measured at this tip: present on 340 pools, absent on 368 — exactly the RESOLVED / WIRING-UNRESOLVED split, and on the 368 the composer keeps its documented one-fact default, unchanged.

notMechanisms.id: poolMeta.role and the render half generally
notMechanisms.what: role, relation, form, move, explains, spines, covers
notMechanisms.why: they select which CANDIDATES exist and how one seats, which is a mechanism of composition and not of the DRAW: `drawVariant` reads `blockId` and `poolKey` and never a pool's fields, so a poolMeta edit cannot move a spine's index by construction (ARCH §2.1). Where one of them changes what a page says it does so through `attach-set` and `registry-id`, which ARE rows above.

notMechanisms.id: grammar and vid on a variant
notMechanisms.what: the `[grammar: Vn]` tag and the minted `vid`
notMechanisms.why: per-variant DATA that no reader of the draw consults. `variantIsAnchored` reads `slots`, `variantIsAudible` reads `marks`, and neither reads `grammar` or `vid` (GRAMMAR_TAG_CONTRACT.seedSafe). `vids` IS a row above, because a RENUMBERING is refused; carrying the number is not.

notMechanisms.what: poolMeta.seat and its seatReason / seatRow — the SEAT LICENCE, resolved at projection from the wiring census's reads, the 165 relation rows and the three ratified aliases (SEAM car 4d), and read by the composer in place of the spine's primary field
notMechanisms.why: IT IS NOT A MECHANISM OF THIS REGISTER AT THIS TIP, and that is a measurement rather than a judgment: the licence resolves to `sentence` on all 708 pools with the reason `not-a-modifier` on every one, so no value of it reaches a draw at all. It is not a modulus, not a key, not an ordering and not an eligibility test — `drawVariant` reads `blockId` and `poolKey` and never a pool's fields (ARCH §2.1) — and what it decides is ARRANGEMENT: which of two seats a modifier takes, and which connective list the joint is drawn from. ⛔ IT BECOMES SHIFT-CLASS THE DAY THE FIRST `consequence` ROW IS LICENSED. A pool moving from `sentence` to `clause` moves the connective draw onto a different list and re-arranges the unit, so the car that lands an alias joining a relation endpoint to a desk read root promotes this row to a mechanism with its pin, its door and its shift class — and the register says so here rather than in a lane's receipt. Until then: the join is 0 of 165 (car 0's F1, re-derived in the projection contract), no shipped pool declares `role: modifier`, and the key is emitted nowhere, because an ABSENT seat reads in the composer as the sentence.
